lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The bakery role appears before the more relevant quant experience.
items.because: It makes the initial impression less focused for a quant-research role.

items.says: There is no brief target-role cue near the top.
items.because: Readers must infer the connection between the statistics, trading, and engineering work.

items.says: Six bullets give the three-month Northpeak internship too much space.
items.because: The section has overlap and a potentially problematic Sharpe claim.

items.says: “Within budget” needs scale or a measurable outcome.
items.because: It does not convey the scale or outcome of the responsibility.

items.says: Use the US spelling “labor” instead of “labour.”
items.because: The document should use consistent US spelling.

items.says: The period over which unsold bread fell is unclear.
Clarify whether the change from 12% to 7% is stated in percentage points or as a relative reduction.
The bakery role could take less space relative to quant work.
items.because: Quant work is more relevant to the target role.

items.says: Define “risk-adjusted returns” and give the comparison baseline.
items.because: The 35% improvement is currently hard to evaluate.

items.says: Give the evaluation period for the 35% improvement.
items.because: The result is currently hard to evaluate.

items.says: Say whether the 35% improvement was backtested or live.
items.because: The result is currently hard to evaluate.

items.says: Explain what the validation was applied to.
Explain how costs were handled in the validation.
Clarify your individual contribution to the feature store.
Clarify what reuse in two later projects meant in practice.
Distinguish approval for an allocation from actual deployment or live performance.
items.because: The current wording does not say whether the allocation went live.

items.says: Explain how selection bias from choosing among 400 configurations was addressed.
items.because: The selection process can inflate the best backtest result.

items.says: Do not present the best backtest Sharpe as expected live Sharpe without a defensible basis.
items.because: The selected backtest result may be inflated by multiple testing and overfitting.

items.says: The 18-month order-book-imbalance result overlaps with the Kaggle claim.
items.because: If it is the same work, repeating it makes the résumé look padded.

items.says: Clarify what the Sharpe comparison measures.
Define the 18-month out-of-sample period.
Verify and accurately describe the random-number setup.
items.because: Giving every worker the same seed can produce duplicate streams and compromise the study.

items.says: Clarify your authorship and contribution to the paper.
Give the paper’s title, author list, and publication status rather than relying on “now Section 3.”
items.because: “Now Section 3” is less informative to an outside reader.

items.says: Reduce or omit the teaching detail if space is limited.
items.because: It is less relevant than research, coding, and trading evidence for most quant-research roles.

items.says: Add measurement context for the 3,000 downloads.
items.because: The review asks what the count covers and when it was measured.

items.says: Make the R package’s relevance to the target role apparent.
State the comparison period for the 7% QLIKE improvement.
items.because: Readers will want to know that the benchmark and evaluation setup are comparable.

items.says: Explain how the 7% improvement is aggregated across indices.
items.because: Readers will want to know how the result was evaluated across the 30 indices.

items.says: Identify and define “both crisis periods.”
Add a concrete result, placement, or distinctive contribution to the generic Kaggle bullet.
items.because: Feature engineering and gradient boosting alone contribute little.

items.says: Do not treat the smaller validation-to-leaderboard gap alone as proof that leakage was removed.
items.because: A smaller score gap does not, by itself, establish that.

items.says: Explain which leakage risk the time-grouped split addressed.
The order-book-imbalance result appears to duplicate the Northpeak achievement.
items.because: If it is the same work, retaining both claims could undermine trust.

items.says: Support Kafka with an experience bullet or remove it if experience is limited.
items.because: No experience bullet currently shows how you used it.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: The visible proofreading error may interfere with keyword matching.

items.says: Reconsider the short methods list so it reflects your strongest demonstrated capabilities.
items.because: It omits some research and validation methods shown elsewhere.
